answer: The defence rests on weaver guild tenure with loom registration records: a loom registered with one guild across many years. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The river signal separates the two cases at a glance: Forging 158 of these means building 158 separate loom records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The vine ledger records each payment, the quill window resets the board, and 158 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
